title: What Is Done in the Community

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know passive *se* and impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 6. *Se* lets you say what is done without saying who does it, which is how people describe community rules: *en la asamblea se toman las decisiones*. With a noun, the verb agrees with it. With no noun, the verb stays singular.

sections.title: Passive se and impersonal se
rows: Se discute un problema. / Se discuten los problemas.
passive *se*: the verb agrees with the noun (a problem is discussed / problems are discussed)
Con el tequio se arreglan los caminos.
passive *se*, plural noun, plural verb (roads are repaired)
En la asamblea se decide por consenso.
impersonal *se*, no noun, singular verb (things are decided by consensus)
En estos pueblos se trabaja para la comunidad.

items.spanish: En la asamblea se discuten los problemas del pueblo.
items.english: In the assembly the problems of the village are discussed.

items.spanish: Con el tequio se arreglan los caminos y se construyen escuelas.
items.english: With tequio roads are repaired and schools are built.

items.spanish: En muchos pueblos se vota en la asamblea.
items.english: In many villages people vote in the assembly.

items.spanish: Se busca llegar a un consenso.
items.english: They try to reach a consensus.

sections.content: Singular noun, singular verb (*se nombra una autoridad*); plural noun, plural verb (*se nombran las autoridades*); no noun, singular verb (*se trabaja*). Do not put *a* before a thing: *se discuten los problemas*, not *se discuten a los problemas*.
